fixture: native-nosbom-1.1.0 (paired against native-sbom-1.1.0, which bundles the same library and covers it)
note: The wheel bundles a shared library (`greetlib/_speedups.abi3.so` and `greetlib/libs/libgreet-2.1.so`) and ships no `.dist-info/sboms/` directory. This is the phantom-dependency case the check exists for: a pip-level scan of this wheel sees greetlib 1.1.0 and nothing else, exactly as it did for the cryptography wheels that re-released solely to bundle a patched OpenSSL. The paired control is what makes the finding mean something - it bundles the SAME library and passes, so a linter cannot earn this case by reporting on any wheel with a .so in it.

must_report_on.evidence_note: MIRI-PY-024's violation_unit is `the wheel's SBOM state` - one violation per wheel, not per bundled library - so the document-only form is what lint-report-v1 sanctions here.

must_not_report_on.note: Bundles the same two .so files and ships a CycloneDX document covering libgreet, listed in RECORD.

why_this_case_was_missing: MIRI-PY-024 is a MUST worth 4 weight and had no artifact at all: every arm in the suite was pure Python, so the check was never even applicable, let alone falsified.
